faq.a: Migration is moving from one place to live in another, either within a country or to a new country. A person who moves into a country to live is called an immigrant; leaving is emigrating.

faq.q: Why do people move to a new country?
faq.a: Push factors drive people away, like no jobs, danger or drought. Pull factors draw them in, like jobs, safety, education or family already there. Most moves mix both.
asks: Tell me about mum's new job
What are push and pull factors?

faq.q: Why is saying goodbye hard when you move?
faq.a: You leave behind people and places you love, like grandparents, friends and familiar food. Feeling sad is normal, and many families keep in touch by phone and video calls.
asks: Is it sad to move away?

faq.q: What is hard about starting at a new school in a new country?
faq.a: There may be a new language, new rules, different food and weather, and no friends at first. It can feel lonely and confusing until things become familiar.

faq.q: How do people settle into a new country?
faq.a: Little by little: learning the language, making friends, finding local places and sharing their own culture. Kind neighbours and classmates make a big difference.
asks: How can I welcome a new classmate?

facts: The UN counted about 281 million international migrants in 2020, roughly 3.6 percent of the world's people.
The Philippines is one of the world's largest sources of nurses working abroad.

quiz.say: A family moves because there is a drought on their farm. Is that a push or a pull factor?
quiz.show: A drought at home is a…
quiz.why: A drought drives people away from home, so it is a push factor.

wrong.0: Pull factors attract people to the new place, like jobs there.
wrong.2: Drought is a common reason people leave, so it counts.
